 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Oct 22, 2026, 12:07:17 IST SUMMARY India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st T20I: India will look to overcome travel fatigue and make a winning start to their five-match T20I series against New Zealand in the opening match on Thursday. Led by Shreyas Iyer, the visitors will depend on their strong batting line-up, but the relatively inexperienced squad has had barely two days to rest, adjust to the conditions and train. 
 India have won their last two T20I series in New Zealand and will aim to continue that run. However, the pace-friendly conditions and the absence of key players could make the opening match a challenging test. 
 India's most recent T20I match on New Zealand soil came in 2022 in Napier. The rain-hit game ended in a tie under the Duckworth-Lewis method. India, however, won the series after claiming victory in the only match that was not affected by bad weather. 
 Only four batters in India's current squad have previously played T20Is in New Zealand. They are captain Iyer, Ishan Kishan, Sanju Samson and Shivam Dube. 
 Abhishek Sharma, Tilak Varma and 15-year-old sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi bring plenty of firepower to the batting line-up. However, they will need to adjust to the nippy weather and conditions that can help seam bowlers. 
 For Iyer, the series offers an opportunity to prove himself in difficult overseas conditions. His tenure as captain began with back-to-back defeats in Ireland and England. 
 Squads 
 India: Shreyas Iyer (c), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan, Tilak Varma, Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav. 
 New Zealand: Mitchell Santner (c), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Mark Chapman, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Lockie Ferguson, Zak Foulkes, Matt Henry, Bevon Jacobs, Kyle Jamieson, Adam Milne, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Tim Seifert, Nathan Smith. Commentary

 12:04 (IST) Oct 22 The captain of New Zealand - Mitchell Santner says they would have bowled first as well. Notes that it's a fresh pitch and they will now look to put a big score on the board. On the team coming back together after a while, Santner says it has been good, though pretty busy. Santner says the guys have gotten back into camp and are really excited for a big series, calling an all-three-format tour against India a cool one. He notes that a lot of the players have been playing overseas and training, but everyone is ready to go now. On the team combination, Santner notes that a couple of guys are not here, but feels the depth they have at the moment is really good. He confirms that Duffy, Kyle Jamieson and Conway miss out, and says they are going with four seamers. On Daryl Mitchell batting at three and Bevon Jacobs getting an opportunity at five, Santner says Jacobs has shown what he can do for a period of time now. He feels Jacobs has the power and is a very good middle-order player, and calls it a good series for him to test himself against a very good team on some good wickets.

 12:04 (IST) Oct 22 The Indian captain - Shreyas Iyer opts to bowl first, citing the quick turnaround, and they want to get an idea of how the wicket is playing. Shares that some of the players took a little time to get accustomed to the conditions and the time difference, but there are no complaints, as they are all professionals. Iyer believes that there were plenty of positives with both bat and ball from the West Indies series, and he wants the team to carry the same attitude into this series. Informs that they have two changes from the last game against West Indies in Bengaluru, with Nitish Kumar Reddy and Mayank Yadav coming into the side.
 12:02 (IST) Oct 22 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st T20I: India opt to bowl India skipper Shreyas Iyer wins the toss, opts to bowl against New Zealand in Christchurch 11:48 (IST) Oct 22 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st T20I: Ishan Kishan aims to break Rizwan's world record Ishan Kishan is also closing in on the record for the most T20I runs in a calendar year by a batter from a Test-playing nation.
 Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan holds the record with 1,326 runs in 29 innings in 2021, including one century and 12 fifties. Kishan needs another 139 runs to surpass that tally.
 Kishan eyes 2,000 T20 runs in a calendar year
 Kishan has been equally prolific in T20 cricket overall. In 49 T20 matches this year, he has scored 1,760 runs in 49 innings at an average of 38.26 and a strike rate of over 175. His tally includes one century and 13 fifties.
 With five T20Is against New Zealand and a three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka in December still to come, Kishan needs 240 more runs to become the first Indian to score 2,000 T20 runs in a calendar year.
 Only West Indies star Nicholas Pooran, who scored 2,331 runs in 76 matches, and Rizwan, who scored 2,036 runs in 48 matches in 2024 and 2021, respectively, have achieved the feat.

 11:36 (IST) Oct 22 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st T20I: Kishan closing in on 2,000 T20I runs Ishan Kishan has scored 1,954 runs in 66 T20I innings at an average of 31.51 and a strike rate of 148.81. His tally includes one century and 13 fifties, with a highest score of 103.
 He needs 46 more runs to reach the 2,000-run mark in the shortest format for India.
 Seven runs away from breaking Suryakumar's record
 Kishan has enjoyed an impressive year in T20Is. In 34 matches and innings this year, he has scored 1,158 runs at an average of 37.35 and a strike rate of 172.06. His tally includes one century and seven fifties.
 He is just seven runs away from surpassing Suryakumar's record of 1,164 T20I runs in a calendar year, set in 2022. Achieving the milestone would make Kishan the Indian batter with the most T20I runs in a single calendar year.

 11:10 (IST) Oct 22 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st T20I: New Zealand have plenty of pace options New Zealand have a variety of pace options for the expected conditions, with Jacob Duffy, Matt Henry, Adam Milne, Lockie Ferguson, Kyle Jamieson and Blair Tickner giving Santner several choices.
 Despite the jet lag and limited preparation time, India will start as overwhelming favourites.
 The two countries are celebrating 100 years of sporting ties this year. The T20I series will be followed by a five-match ODI series and two Tests.

 11:00 (IST) Oct 22 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st T20I: Santner expects both teams to adapt New Zealand captain Santner expects conditions to change as the series moves across the country. He believes offering flat pitches to India's power-packed batting line-up may not be the best approach.
 Santner will hope his own big-hitters, including Glenn Phillips and Finn Allen, can match the Indian stars.
 The injury-forced absence of Rachin Ravindra has also opened the door for veteran Devon Conway to move up the batting order.
 "If there is something in the pitch for the seamers to start, it's obviously nice, but throughout the series we're going around the country, they're not all going to be green seamers and flying around. So both teams are going to have to adapt quickly to the conditions and then play accordingly," Santner said.
 10:55 (IST) Oct 22 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st T20I: India's T20 reboot begins amid travel fatigue, tight schedule and bowling concerns
 It’s been barely 48 hours since India landed in Christchurch after taking a flight out of Bengaluru. Shreyas Iyer and his men will be forgiven for still being sleep-deprived and jet-lagged when they walk out at Hagley Oval for the first of five T20Is against New Zealand today. 
Indian cricketers are conditioned to relentless travel, but that does not make the grind any less demanding. The modern cricket calendar is shaped more by commercial interests and diplomatic necessities and less by sporting logic and priorities. 
This tour is a case study. 
Stretching over 43 days, the visit marks a century of sporting ties between India and New Zealand, a relationship that dates back to the great Major Dhyan Chand leading an Indian Army hockey team to the country in 1926. 
It also offers New Zealand crowds a rare chance to watch Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma when the five-match ODI series follows the T20Is from Nov 4. He needs just 46 runs to become the seventh Indian player to score 2,000 runs in T20Is.
 The left-hander is also on the verge of breaking Suryakumar Yadav's record for the most T20I runs by an Indian in a calendar year. Kishan, who has been in sensational form at number three, will get his first opportunity in the series opener in Christchurch on Thursday.

 Their return could help India address some of their bowling concerns. However, questions remain over the abilities of all-rounders Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube.
 India prefer to bat deep, often extending their batting line-up to number eight. They are unlikely to abandon that approach to add more strength to their bowling attack.
 10:22 (IST) Oct 22 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st T20I: Missing Hardik and Bumrah India will be without two proven match-winners. All-rounder Hardik Pandya is injured, while pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah will feature only in the ODI and Test series on this tour.
 Pandya had led India during their 2022 tour of New Zealand.
 Sooryavanshi is likely to warm the bench, but India still have plenty of batting firepower. Abhishek and Samson impressed during the home series against the West Indies.
 Iyer has admitted that bowling is the area India need to improve.
 10:22 (IST) Oct 22 India vs New Zealand Live Score, 1st T20I: Iyer faces a challenging away assignment For Iyer, the series offers an opportunity to prove himself in difficult overseas conditions. His tenure as captain began with back-to-back defeats in Ireland and England.
 Mitchell Santner's New Zealand will look to put Iyer and his team under pressure. India arrive after winning gold for the second successive time at the Asian Games and playing out a hard-fought drawn home series against the West Indies.
 If the New Zealand series follows the pattern of India's tour of the UK earlier this year, the pressure on Iyer could increase. He is expected to lead India at the T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand in two years' time.
 Iyer, however, sounded confident about his team's ability to adapt to different conditions. India travelled soon after sharing the home series against the West Indies.
